findings.description: The new `not-mounted` branch turns every `Missing` failure into an informational counter whenever `.loa/.claude` is a directory and the manifest path exists under `.loa/<path>`. In a submodule mount every manifest path exists under `.loa/` by construction, so the condition is always true: deleting any managed System Zone file (a hook such as implement-gate, a gate script, a protocol file) no longer fails the integrity check. The removed file's hash is never compared against `.loa/<path>` either, so there is no verification that the upstream copy is intact. Combined with the new unconditional `return 0` at the end of the function (line 87), the function can no longer signal drift through its exit status; any caller that relied on `check_integrity` returning non-zero on tampering is now silenced.
findings.failure_mode: An agent or compromised process removes a guard file from `.claude/` on a submodule mount. `check-loa.sh` prints one `not-mounted: N path(s)` line and reports success; the fence the file implemented is gone without a Tampered/Missing failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat a path as legitimately not-mounted when it is absent from the mount's own link set (e.g. consult the mount manifest/scope list that sandbox-mount.sh or the mount tool records), not merely because it exists under `.loa/`. For paths that are expected to be linked, keep `fail "Missing"`. Drop the trailing `return 0` or return `[[ $drift == false ]]` so callers can observe drift.

findings.description: The manifest tree is derived by following the `.claude/checksums.json` symlink with `readlink` and then running `git -C <that dir> ls-files`. The symlink target is not constrained to the project or the `.loa/` submodule, so whoever controls the link chooses which git tree the file count is taken from, which lets them make the count match an arbitrary manifest. Running `git` inside an attacker-chosen directory also honours that repository's `.git/config` (e.g. `core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`), which is a known command-execution vector for git operations on untrusted repos. The pre-existing count check is weak, so this is a hardening concern rather than a direct bypass.
findings.failure_mode: A tampered symlink points `checksums.json` at a foreign tree whose tracked `.claude/` count matches the forged manifest; preflight reports no mismatch. A planted repo config at the link target could run commands when git is invoked.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the link with `realpath` and require the result to be inside `${PROJECT_ROOT}` or `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.loa` before using it; otherwise fall back to the legacy count and warn. Consider `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` plus `-c core.fsmonitor= -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` when running git in a derived directory.

findings.description: The script's header states the arm is never read from `sandbox/` because the sandbox is agent-writable (DEC-0413), yet the dissent envelopes that drive `voices_run`, the DEGRADED check and part of `degraded_reason` are read first from `$RUN_DIR/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-*.json`. The agent under evaluation (or prompt-injected content it processes) can write or rewrite that file to report `voices_succeeded == voices_planned` and `status: FULL`, hiding a degraded or skipped gate from the runs.jsonl row. The eval-owned copy under `eval/` is only used as a fallback.
findings.failure_mode: A run whose review/audit voices failed is recorded as non-degraded because the sandbox copy of the envelope was forged or edited by the agent, skewing ablation results.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the harness-owned copy under `$RUN_DIR/eval/` and only fall back to the sandbox path when the harness did not capture one; or have pipeline-run.sh copy the envelope out of the sandbox at phase end and record its sha256 so ablation-row.sh can verify it.

findings.description: `zone_violations.dot_claude_writes` only inspects `Write`/`Edit`/`MultiEdit`/`NotebookEdit` tool_use blocks whose `file_path` matches `(^|/)\.claude/`. Writes performed through the `Bash` tool (redirects, `sed -i`, `cp`, `mv`) and paths that reach `.claude/` via `..` or symlinks are not counted, so the metric under-reports System Zone writes. This mirrors the accepted Bash-path fence gap in CLAUDE.loa.md but the row schema presents the count as authoritative.
findings.failure_mode: An arm that edits `.claude/` through Bash shows zero zone violations in runs.jsonl.
findings.suggested_fix: Also scan Bash tool inputs for `.claude/` tokens (heuristic flag), or compare the sandbox's `.claude/` tree against its pre-run snapshot in pipeline-run.sh and record the diff; document the metric as Write/Edit-tool only in the schema.

findings.description: When `bats` is not on PATH the script defaults to executing `$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats --version`, an operator-specific path baked into a shared harness script. Any file at that path is executed; the `tool_version` helper also runs `$EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN` and `$LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` from the environment without restriction. These are development conveniences, but a personal home-directory path in committed code is a hardening smell and a `--version` call on an arbitrary executable runs it.
findings.failure_mode: On a host where that path exists but is writable by another user or populated by an unrelated checkout, fingerprint.sh executes it; on other hosts the fingerprint silently reads `bats=absent`, hiding the toolchain difference.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the personal-path default and require `--bats-bin`/`LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` or PATH; record `bats=absent` otherwise.

findings.cross_file_justification: The codex-headless hop (cli_model at line 240) now prices through this placeholder entry; cost estimates feed the spend ledger and spend.sh caps touched in this change set, and ablation-row.sh sums ledger_cost_usd from the same MODELINV rows.
findings.description: The new `gpt-6.1-sol` entry carries copied gpt-5.5 prices explicitly marked PLACEHOLDER, and the codex-headless hop was repointed to it, so every Codex CLI estimate and MODELINV row for the default OpenAI CLI path is now priced with unconfirmed numbers. If the real gpt-6.1 rate card is higher, spend caps and budget enforcement computed from estimates under-count, and ablation cost comparisons between arms are biased.
findings.failure_mode: Spend-cap checks pass while actual subscription/API usage exceeds the intended budget; cost_usd in runs.jsonl is systematically wrong for the codex path.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the entry `cost_estimated`/`pricing_confidence: placeholder` in the catalog so ledger rows and spend.sh can surface it, and close the bead confirming the rate card before relying on these estimates for caps.

findings.description: The `@loa-managed` header version changed (rc.3 → rc.5 in the diff, rc.6 in the current file) while the recorded content hash `a7a0470c…` stayed identical across all three versions. Either the hash does not cover the header (so version drift is unverifiable) or it is stale. Tools that trust this hash to detect edits to the managed instruction file get no signal from this change.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream managed-file verification accepts a modified CLAUDE.loa.md because the header hash is not regenerated with the content.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the header hash whenever the managed file (including the version field) changes, or document that the hash covers only the body and add a check that the version matches `.loa-version.json`.
